response.title: backup power for an electric fence charger
response.answer:
For an electric fence charger (energizer), there are three practical backup power options, depending on whether your charger runs on 120V AC or 12V DC.

Backup option

	

Best for

	

Typical backup duration




12V deep-cycle battery

	

12V-compatible fence chargers

	

1–7+ days




UPS battery backup

	

120V plug-in fence chargers

	

A few hours to 1+ day




Solar panel + battery

	

Remote fences or extended outages

	

Potentially continuous with sufficient sunlight

Recommended setups
Shop

1. 12V battery backup

Best for chargers with a 12V DC input. A 20Ah LiFePO4 battery stores about 256Wh and can power a 5W energizer for roughly 40 hours after allowing for losses.

Shop

2. UPS backup

Easiest for an existing 120V AC fence charger. Plug the charger into a compatible UPS, which automatically switches to battery during an outage. Check its runtime at the charger's actual wattage.

Shop

3. Solar battery system

Ideal for longer outages. A solar panel, charge controller, and battery can maintain fence operation without grid power when sized for local sunlight and energy consumption.

How much battery capacity do you need?

For example, with a charger consuming 5 watts:

Battery capacity

	

Approximate runtime*




12V 10Ah

	

19 hours




12V 20Ah

	

38 hours




12V 50Ah

	

96 hours




12V 100Ah

	

192 hours

*Assumes LiFePO4 batteries, approximately 80% usable capacity, and 5W continuous consumption. Actual runtime varies by charger and system losses.

One important consideration: Do not connect a battery directly to a mains-only fence charger. Use a compatible UPS or manufacturer-approved battery power system, and preserve the energizer's required grounding and isolation.

markup:
For an **electric fence charger (energizer)**, there are three practical backup power options, depending on whether your charger runs on 120V AC or 12V DC.

| Backup option | Best for | Typical backup duration |
|---|---|---|
| **12V deep-cycle battery** | 12V-compatible fence chargers | 1–7+ days |
| **UPS battery backup** | 120V plug-in fence chargers | A few hours to 1+ day |
| **Solar panel + battery** | Remote fences or extended outages | Potentially continuous with sufficient sunlight |

## Recommended setups

<box gap={3}>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="12 volt LiFePO4 deep cycle battery 20Ah" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="124px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **1. 12V battery backup**

      Best for chargers with a 12V DC input. A 20Ah LiFePO4 battery stores about 256Wh and can power a 5W energizer for roughly 40 hours after allowing for losses.
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="APC UPS battery backup 600VA power supply" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="124px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **2. UPS backup**

      Easiest for an existing 120V AC fence charger. Plug the charger into a compatible UPS, which automatically switches to battery during an outage. Check its runtime at the charger's actual wattage.
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="solar electric fence energizer battery solar panel outdoor farm" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="124px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **3. Solar battery system**

      Ideal for longer outages. A solar panel, charge controller, and battery can maintain fence operation without grid power when sized for local sunlight and energy consumption.
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

## How much battery capacity do you need?

For example, with a charger consuming 5 watts:

| Battery capacity | Approximate runtime* |
|---|---|
| 12V 10Ah | 19 hours |
| 12V 20Ah | 38 hours |
| 12V 50Ah | 96 hours |
| 12V 100Ah | 192 hours |

<caption>*Assumes LiFePO4 batteries, approximately 80% usable capacity, and 5W continuous consumption. Actual runtime varies by charger and system losses.</caption>

**One important consideration:** Do not connect a battery directly to a mains-only fence charger. Use a compatible UPS or manufacturer-approved battery power system, and preserve the energizer's required grounding and isolation.

{@body const [model,setModel] = DIL.useState("")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Recommend a backup power setup for my electric fence charger. Power source: "+power+". Desired runtime: "+duration+". Brand/model: "+(model||"Unknown")+". Include compatible options and estimated battery size.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Charger power source</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={power} onChange={setPower}>
        <radio value="120V AC plug-in">120V AC (wall outlet)</radio>
        <radio value="12V DC battery">12V DC (battery powered)</radio>
        <radio value="Unknown">Not sure</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Desired backup duration</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={duration} onChange={setDuration}>
        <radio value="8 hours">8 hours</radio>
        <radio value="24 hours">24 hours</radio>
        <radio value="3 days">3 days</radio>
        <radio value="7+ days">7+ days</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Charger brand/model (optional)</label>
      <input value={model} onChange={setModel} placeholder="e.g., Gallagher, Zareba, Parmak"/>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Find a suitable backup setup <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>
